stories.headline: Xi and Putin hail ties at 'historic high' in Beijing, extend friendship treaty days after Trump visit

key_facts.fact: Xi Jinping hosted Vladimir Putin in Beijing on May 20, with Xi declaring China-Russia relations at a 'historic high' and a 'new stage', just days after Xi hosted US President Trump in China.
key_facts.excerpt: China-Russia relations are at a 'historic high,' Chinese leader Xi Jinping said Wednesday as he met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Beijing days after he hosted U.S. President Donald Trump.

key_facts.fact: The two leaders oversaw the signing of more than 40 cooperation agreements spanning trade, technology, energy and media, and agreed to extend the 2001 Sino-Russian Treaty of Friendship.
key_facts.excerpt: Putin and Xi oversaw the signing of more than 40 cooperation agreements in areas such as trade, technology and media exchanges. They stressed their growing trade, particularly in oil and natural gas.

key_facts.fact: Bilateral trade reached nearly $240 billion in 2025, with China Russia's largest trading partner for 16 years running; nearly all Russia-China import-export transactions are now settled in rubles and yuan.
key_facts.excerpt: In 2025, our trade reached nearly US$240 billion... nearly all Russia-China export-import transactions are made in rubles and yuan. In other words, we have actually created a stable system of mutual trade that is protected from external influence.

key_facts.fact: The leaders signed a joint declaration on a 'multipolar world' and reached an understanding on the long-delayed Power of Siberia 2 gas pipeline, which would carry 50 billion cubic metres of Russian gas annually to China via Mongolia, though details remain under negotiation.
key_facts.excerpt: The Kremlin said on Wednesday that an understanding had been reached for the route and construction of the long-delayed joint Siberia 2 pipeline, but details are still being negotiated. Once completed, the pipeline will transport 50 billion cubic metres of Russian gas annually to China via Mongolia.

key_facts.fact: The Russia-China joint statement took aim at Trump's $175 billion 'Golden Dome' missile-defense plan and criticized the expiry of the last US-Russia arms control treaty.
key_facts.excerpt: In a joint statement, China and Russia took [aim] at US President Donald Trump's plans for a $175bn 'Golden Dome' defence system... The duo also criticised the expiry of the last US-Russia arms control treaty.

stories.headline: Iran reviews new US peace proposal as Trump says talks 'on the borderline'; CENTCOM boards Iranian tanker

key_facts.fact: Iran said on May 20 it was examining a new US proposal to end the Middle East war, conveyed via mediators, as Trump described negotiations as on the 'borderline' between a deal and renewed strikes and in their 'final stages'.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran said on May 20 that it was examining a new US proposal to end the Middle East war, as US President Donald Trump described the talks as being on the 'borderline' between a deal and renewed strikes.

key_facts.fact: Trump said he was ready to proceed with further attacks on Iran if it did not agree to a deal, but suggested he could wait a few days to 'get the right answers'.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. President Donald Trump on Wednesday said he was ready to proceed with further attacks on Iran if it did not agree to a peace deal, but suggested he could wait a few days to 'get the right answers.'

key_facts.fact: Trump and Netanyahu held a tense phone call; Netanyahu was highly skeptical of a Qatar/Pakistan-drafted 'letter of intent' that would officially end the war and open 30 days of negotiations on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and limiting Iran's nuclear program.
key_facts.excerpt: The emerging proposal - reportedly drafted by Qatar and Pakistan... would see Washington and Tehran sign a 'letter of intent' that would officially end the war and open 30 days of negotiations on issues including reopening the Strait of Hormuz and limiting Iran's nuclear program.

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said Marines boarded an Iranian-flagged oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman on May 20 on suspicion it was trying to violate the US counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
key_facts.excerpt: US Central Command (CENTCOM) said Marines boarded an Iranian-flagged oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman on May 20 on suspicion it was trying to violate the restrictions.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority announced a new oversight zone in the Strait of Hormuz requiring transiting vessels to coordinate with Iranian authorities; Tehran said the US had failed to reopen the strait despite 'tricks'.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority announced a new oversight zone in the Strait of Hormuz requiring vessels transiting designated areas to coordinate with Iranian authorities.

key_facts.fact: A ceasefire reached on April 8 through Pakistani mediation halted open fighting, but has not reopened the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of the world's oil and LNG normally passes.
key_facts.excerpt: The ceasefire halted the fighting but has not reopened the Strait of Hormuz, the vital waterway that normally carries about a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas.

stories.headline: Fed minutes show majority open to a rate hike as Iran-war inflation bites, ahead of Warsh's arrival

key_facts.fact: Minutes of the Fed's April 28-29 meeting, released May 20, showed a majority of policymakers felt 'some policy firming would likely become appropriate' if inflation continues to run persistently above the 2% target.
key_facts.excerpt: A majority of Fed policymakers at their April 28-29 meeting felt 'some policy firming would likely become appropriate' if inflation stays persistently above the central bank's 2 per cent target, according to minutes of the meeting released Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: The FOMC left its policy rate unchanged in a range of 3.50%-3.75%, but four policymakers dissented - the most since 1992.
key_facts.excerpt: The Federal Open Market Committee, the Fed's rate-setting body, left its short-term policy rate unchanged in a range of 3.50% to 3.75% last month, but four policymakers dissented, the most since 1992.

key_facts.fact: The Fed's preferred PCE inflation gauge was estimated at 3.5% in March, up from 2.8% in February, as the Iran war disrupted Middle East energy supplies.
key_facts.excerpt: The minutes indicated that the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, was estimated at 3.5% in March. That's well above the Fed's 2% inflation target and jumped from 2.8% in February as the Iran war disrupted energy supplies.

key_facts.fact: The conflict has sent oil prices up by more than 50%; incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh inherits an increasingly hawkish committee.
key_facts.excerpt: The conflict has sent oil prices up by more than 50%, and the latest consumer and wholesale inflation data show price pressures have begun widening beyond the energy sector... incoming Chair Kevin Warsh will inherit an increasingly hawkish crew of central bankers.

key_facts.fact: Markets now see the Fed's next move as a possible hike rather than a cut; before the war they had priced in two 2026 rate cuts.
key_facts.excerpt: Before the United States and Israel launched the war in February, markets had priced in two interest rate cuts for 2026... The Fed is now not expected to change rates until late in the year -- after which the next move is expected to be a hike.

stories.headline: US gas prices near record over Memorial Day as Hormuz closure threatens $200 oil

key_facts.fact: The US national average gas price is expected to reach about $4.48 a gallon over Memorial Day weekend - 42% above last Memorial Day and the second-highest on record, according to GasBuddy.
key_facts.excerpt: GasBuddy... expects the national average will be about $4.48 a gallon this Memorial Day. That would be 42% above the price last Memorial Day and the second-highest on record.

key_facts.fact: Analysts warn the national average could hit $5 a gallon next month if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed; only 21% of Americans approve of Trump's handling of gas prices.
key_facts.excerpt: Patrick De Haan, GasBuddy's head of petroleum analysis, told CNN he expects the national average for regular gas will hit $5 a gallon at some point next month if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed... Just 21% of Americans approve of President Trump's handling of gas prices.

key_facts.fact: US commercial and emergency oil inventories plunged by the most on record last week, and the Strategic Petroleum Reserve has declined 10% since the war started, to a two-year low.
key_facts.excerpt: US commercial and emergency oil inventories plunged by the most on record last week... The amount of oil in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve has declined 10% since the war started to the lowest level in two years.

key_facts.fact: Wood Mackenzie warned a prolonged Strait of Hormuz closure is the single greatest threat to global energy markets in decades, with Brent potentially approaching $200/bbl in a worst case; more than 11 million b/d of Gulf crude and around 20% of global LNG supply are curtailed.
key_facts.excerpt: Oil prices could reach US$200/bbl in worst-case scenario as more than 11 million b/d of Gulf crude and condensate supply remains curtailed... over 80 million tonnes per annum (Mtpa) of LNG supply, equivalent to around 20% of global supply, remains inaccessible.

key_facts.fact: Oil prices spiked back above $100 per barrel as of May 20, remaining extremely volatile on conflicting signals about a US-Iran deal.
key_facts.excerpt: Prices have been extremely volatile, spiking back above $100 per barrel as of May 20.

stories.headline: SpaceX files publicly for what would be the largest IPO ever, revealing $4.9B 2025 loss

key_facts.fact: SpaceX publicly disclosed its IPO filing on May 20, set to be the largest IPO in history; it plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker 'SPCX', with a debut expected in late June.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX on Wednesday disclosed its filing for an initial public offering... SpaceX is expected to begin trading in late June on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol 'SPCX.'

key_facts.fact: SpaceX reported a net loss of $4.9 billion on $18.67 billion in revenue for 2025, swinging from a $791 million profit on $14.0 billion in revenue in 2024, as it invested heavily in xAI's AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX swung to a $4.94 billion consolidated loss in 2025 on revenue of $18.67 billion as it invested heavily in xAI's artificial intelligence infrastructure, from a $791 million profit and $14.02 billion in revenue the year before.

key_facts.fact: In Q1 2026 SpaceX booked a $4.3 billion net loss on $4.69 billion in revenue, and disclosed a debt load of $29.1 billion through the first quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: In the first quarter of 2026, SpaceX posted a net loss of $4.3 billion on $4.7 billion in revenue... It also disclosed a debt load through the first quarter of $29.1 billion.

key_facts.fact: Starlink had about 10.3 million subscribers across 164 countries with more than 9,600 satellites by Q1 2026, and accounted for nearly 70% of SpaceX's revenue last year.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet business accounted for nearly 70% of the company's revenue last year... through the first quarter of this year the business had about 10.3 million subscribers in 164 countries, with more than 9,600 satellites deployed.

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk holds 85.1% of combined voting power through a dual-class stock structure; the offering targets a valuation of roughly $1.75 trillion and a raise of up to $75 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk... will maintain majority control of SpaceX through dual-class stock. He currently holds 85.1% of combined voting power, according to the filing... reportedly targeting a valuation of roughly $1.75 trillion in an offering of up to $75 billion.

key_facts.fact: The filing disclosed a $1.25 billion monthly compute contract with Anthropic; the AI segment (xAI plus X) posted a $6.36 billion operating loss on $3.20 billion in revenue in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: The AI segment is xAI plus X (formerly Twitter). It generated $3.20 billion in revenue in 2025 and lost $1.24 billion at the EBITDA line. Operating loss was $6.36 billion.

stories.headline: Intuit to cut 17% of staff, around 3,000 jobs, to refocus on AI

key_facts.fact: Intuit said on May 20 it would cut about 17% of its full-time workforce - roughly 3,000 of about 18,200 employees - to simplify its organizational structure and become 'a faster, leaner, more focused company'.
key_facts.excerpt: On May 20, 2026, the Company announced a plan... to simplify its organizational structure and become a faster, leaner, more focused company. As part of the Plan, the Company will reduce its full-time workforce by approximately 17%.

key_facts.fact: CEO Sasan Goodarzi's memo said the cuts will help the QuickBooks and TurboTax maker focus on bets like baking AI into its products.
key_facts.excerpt: Intuit is letting 17% of its staff go, or about 3,000 people, as it seeks to divert resources toward baking AI into its products... The memo by CEO Sasan Goodarzi said the layoffs are meant to reduce complexity by simplifying the company's corporate structure and help it focus on AI efforts.

key_facts.fact: Intuit expects $300 million to $340 million in restructuring charges, largely cash severance and benefits, recognized mostly in its fourth fiscal quarter ending July 31, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The company estimates $300-$340 million in charges, mainly severance and benefits, largely recorded in Q4 ending July 31, 2026.

key_facts.fact: Intuit also trimmed its annual TurboTax revenue forecast; its shares fell about 14% after the bell amid lingering fears of AI disruption.
key_facts.excerpt: Intuit lowered annual revenue forecast for its tax-filing software, TurboTax, on Wednesday and said it would cut 17% of its full-time workforce, sending its shares down 14% after the bell amid lingering fears of AI disruption.

key_facts.fact: Intuit shares are down more than 40% so far this year amid worries that generative AI could disrupt its tax business, even as the S&P 500 has gained roughly 8%.
key_facts.excerpt: Intuit... hasn't been perceived as a beneficiary of the AI boom, with its shares consistently underperforming in the broader S&P 500 over the past 12 months.

stories.headline: OpenAI prepares to confidentially file for IPO as soon as Friday, eyeing September debut

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is preparing to confidentially file a draft IPO prospectus with the SEC as soon as Friday (May 22), working with banks including Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is preparing to confidentially file a draft of its initial public offering (IPO) prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) as soon as Friday... working with major financial institutions including Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley.

key_facts.fact: The ChatGPT maker is aiming to go public as early as September; OpenAI is valued at more than $850 billion ($852 billion) by private investors.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is aiming to go public as early as September and is working with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley on a draft IPO prospectus... The plan by the ChatGPT maker, which was last valued at $852 billion.

key_facts.fact: The acceleration comes two days after OpenAI fended off Elon Musk's court challenge, with analysts saying resolving that legal overhang removed a major obstacle to an IPO.
key_facts.excerpt: comes two days after it fended off an existential court challenge from Elon Musk... 'Resolving that legal overhang removed a major obstacle to an IPO and likely gave OpenAI the confidence to accelerate its timeline,' IPOX Vice President Kat Liu said.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's filing would land alongside SpaceX's IPO prospectus, forcing portfolio managers to evaluate both blockbuster offerings side by side.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Simultaneous filings also force portfolio managers to evaluate both companies side by side.'

key_facts.fact: Reuters previously reported OpenAI was laying the groundwork to go public in an offering that could value it at up to $1 trillion, aiming to raise at least $60 billion at the low end.
key_facts.excerpt: The Sam Altman-led company was laying the groundwork to go public in an offering that could value it at up to $1 trillion, Reuters had reported in October, with the aim to raise at least $60 billion at the low end.
